ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and continuous screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, authorised signatories, intermediaries, and platform principals against: New Zealand Department of Internal Affairs consolidated sanctions and fugitive lists; United Nations Security Council sanctions resolutions; United States OFAC SDN list; United Kingdom HMT sanctions list; European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; and domestic criminal and financial intelligence databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any politically exposed person, family member, or close associate as defined by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and FATF Recommendations 12 and 22.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register (https://company-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be presented in Latin script and be capable of accurate reproduction on the New Zealand Companies Register. Registration in English is expected; Te Reo Maori names are permissible where not misleading, offensive, or restricted. Foreign-language names require a certified English transliteration and must not mislead as to legal form, ownership, or association with the Crown or any government entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon approval, the name is reserved for 20 working days. A single extension of 20 working days may be requested through the Companies Office before expiry if incorporation is not yet complete. If the name is rejected, the applicant may request reconsideration in writing within 15 working days, stating the legal grounds under sections 20 to 25 of the Companies Act 1993 and addressing the Registrar's stated objection. If reconsideration is refused, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand by way of application for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, ordinarily within 28 days of the final refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for registered-office purposes only if it provides a physical New Zealand street address at which legal documents may be served during normal business hours and is not a post office box. For a licensed equity crowdfunding platform under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, substantive commercial presence in New Zealand is required; a pure mailbox or virtual-only address without a locally resident board, manager, AML/CFT compliance officer, and principal place of business will not satisfy Financial Markets Authority licensing or AML/CFT supervision expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (85%): unannounced physical on-site inspections are expected during the first 12 months of operation due to the High_Risk_Special_License designation, FMC licensing conditions, and AML/CFT Act supervision by the Financial Markets Authority and the Department of Internal Affairs.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12 to 18, section 34, section 127, sections 128 to 149, and section 159 (registration and statutory books); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Part 6 (subpart 4, requirements for crowdfunding service licence) and Financial Markets Conduct Regulations 2014, Part 6, regulations 270 to 300.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Private Bag 92061, Victoria Street West, Auckland 1142, New Zealand; electronic lodgment via the Companies Office Online Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZ-INC Incorporation Application and the shareholders' and directors' consent forms; must be filed electronically through the Companies Office Online portal, accompanied by the company constitution (or default constitution designation) and certificate of compliance for the proposed company name.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: New Zealand imposes no statutory minimum paid-up share capital for incorporation; the Companies Act 1993 requires only that each initial shareholder subscribes at least one share and that the total issued share capital is stated in the incorporation application and initial annual return. No escrow account or capital deposit is required at the Companies Office stage. However, under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (FMC Act) licensing criteria, the applicant crowdfunding portal must demonstrate minimum operational net tangible assets of NZD 200,000 (approximately USD 126,000) or maintain a professional indemnity insurance policy or a trust/custody arrangement as prescribed by FMA conditions, which must be evidenced at the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) licensing stage, not at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CROWDFUNDING VENTURES NZ LIMITED (hereinafter 'the Company'), ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 180(1) OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the Company adopt its constitution and that the directors allot and issue in accordance with the articles, a total of 1,000 ordinary shares at NZD 1.00 each, fully paid or credited, to the initial subscribers as listed in the incorporation application, and that the Register of Shareholders be updated accordingly. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at Level 10, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland 1010, New Zealand, with the register of the Company's statutory records maintained at that address, and that this address be recorded with the Companies Office as the registered office. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that the following persons be and are hereby appointed as inaugural officers of the Company: (a) Jane Anne Whitfield, appointed as Managing Director, responsible for regulatory compliance and the FMA crowdfunding service licence application; (b) Michael James O'Connor, appointed as Chief Financial Officer and Company Secretary, responsible for statutory filings, financial reporting and maintenance of the company register; and (c) Sophia Grace Lee, appointed as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer for the purposes of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, with authority to liaise with the Financial Markets Authority. 4. BANKING AND CUSTODY: RESOLVED that the Company shall open designated commercial bank accounts with Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (ANZ) Auckland branch for the segregated custody of client funds, and that the operation of such accounts be subject to dual signature and RBNZ-custody rules. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorized to complete and execute all consents, declarations, and filings required to give effect to the incorporation and lawful operation of the Company in accordance with the Companies Act 1993 and the FMC Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (www.business.govt.nz / Companies Register online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a real-time availability search on the NZ Companies Office online name registry. Reserve a proposed company name that includes or corresponds to the entity business scope, avoiding any restricted word (e.g., 'bank', 'trust', 'assurance') without FMA or RBNZ content. File an application for name reservation (the name reservation is valid for 20 business days but is automatically assigned upon incorporation). If the intended brand name is associated with crowdfunding activities, obtain a non-objection letter from the Financial Markets Authority if the word 'crowdfunding' is used.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application (electronic)
Written authority from the proposed director for name reservation if applicable
Deed of name consent from the FMA for restricted words (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or prohibited wording, the registry will provide a preliminary notice. The applicant may apply for reconsideration under section 22 of the Companies Act, demonstrating distinctiveness or submitting a new alternative name. A new reservation application may be lodged immediately at no additional cost for a replacement name within the same online session.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local notary public or solicitor, delivered to the Companies Office via the online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution (or adopt the provisions of the Companies Act 1993 as a default constitution). Ensure the constitution incorporates the mandatory conditions for a licensed crowdfunding service under FMC Act subpart 4, including: investor prioritization rules, maximum offer amount per investor NZD 20,000 per 12-month period, and anti-money-laundering responsibilities under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Each director and shareholder must sign a consent form (Form NZ-COD and shareholder consent). The documents are electronically authenticated by the appointed agent.
required_dossiers: Constitution of the company
Form NZ-COD (Consent to act as Director)
Form NZ-SH (Shareholder Consent)
Certificate of compliance for name reservation
Identity and due diligence documentation for each director/shareholder (passport, proof of address) under AML/CFT requirements
Statement of the registered office address (Level 10, Vero Centre, 48 Shortland Street, Auckland)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office electronically queries the documents for inconsistencies (e.g., missing residency authorizations), the applicant receives a 'Notice of Requirement to Provide Further Information' (section 15 of the Companies Act 1993). The applicant has 20 working days to respond by uploading the corrected consent or revised constitution. No additional fee is charged for a first resubmission; extended queries require a fee of NZD 50 (USD 32).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Electronic Lodgment System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the consolidated incorporation application through the Companies Office online portal. Include full registration of the proposed name, the constitution and consents, and the registered office address. Payment of the incorporation fee is processed by credit card or direct debit. The Registrar will automatically validate (sections 15-16) and, upon approval, issue a certificate of incorporation (Form NZ-CERT) with a unique company number (e.g., NZCS999999). Ensure that the company's ultimate beneficial ownership information is registered in accordance with the Companies (Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) Amendment Act (if effective). Post-incorporation, the registry automatically records the directors and shareholders and issues a company extract.
required_dossiers: Incorporation application form (electronic)
Certificate of incorporation (issued by Registrar, to be retained)
Payment receipt of the incorporation fee
AML/CFT verification for beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for non-payment or defective statutory declarations, the applicant may cure by: (i) rectifying the electronic form and resubmitting with an additional NZD 100 (USD 64) expedited filing fee, or (ii) lodging a manual application at the Auckland Companies Office with a two-day ruling period. If the infringement is substantive (such as non-compliant constitution), the Registrar may revoke the certificate within 30 days; the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for relief under section 368 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration and IRD Number / GST Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and the Companies Office Business Gateway
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Automatically, upon incorporation, the Companies Office transmits incorporation data to the IRD. The company must apply for: (i) an IRD number (tax number) issued to the new company; (ii) GST registration if expected annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 (required for a crowdfunding portal due to service fees, and mandatory at Stage 2); (iii) register as an employer under the PAYE scheme (if hiring). The company must also register for the Financial Markets Authority levy under the Financial Markets (Financial Markets Authority Levies) Regulations 2015.
required_dossiers: IRD number application (electronic, IR596)
GST registration form (online, GST101)
Company certificate of incorporation
Directors' personal IRD numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD does not receive the automatic registration, reapply with the certificate of incorporation issued by the Companies Office. If the GST number is delayed due to due diligence queries on non-resident directors, provide certified copies of passports and proof of overseas addresses. The IRD can issue a temporary IRD number within 24 hours of a service visit to the Wellington IRD office, and any discrepancy is remedied within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Markets Authority Crowdfunding Service Licence Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA), Level 5, Ernst & Young Building, 2 Takutai Square, Britomart, Auckland 1010 (application via the FMA licensing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the full FMC Act crowdfunding service licence application under section 506 of the FMC Act and legislation condition requirements. This includes a comprehensive business plan, operational manuals, a compliance and AML/CFT programme reviewed for FMA approval, hardware/software security of the internet-based platform, conflict-of-interest protocols, investor due diligence, and escrow arrangements with a registered bank. Submit the attestation of capital adequacy (net tangible assets of NZD 200,000, or an equivalent guarantee or professional indemnity insurance). The FMA will conduct a
step_by_step_formation_sop.fit and proper: assessment of directors and senior management. Include a copy of the incorporation certificate and constitution.
required_dossiers: Form FMA-1 – Application for Licence to provide a crowd funding service (FMC Act s.506)
Certificate of incorporation and constitution
Business plan and compliance manual
AML/CFT programme and risk assessment under the AML/CFT Act 2009
Capital adequacy certificate / audit (net tangible assets) or professional indemnity insurance policy
Escrow and custody agreement with ANZ Bank
Organisation chart and 'fit and proper' declarations of all directors and senior managers
External audit report of the online platform infrastructure (security accredited, SOC2 or ISO 27001, or equivalent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of an FMA deficiency notice, the applicant is entitled to submit additional information or a revision of the compliance manual within 15 working days. If the licence application is declined under section 508 of the FMC Act, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand (judicial review) and/or file a fresh application with material amendments reflecting FMA guidance. The FMA has internal facilitation meetings available upon written request to expedite queries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Governance and Corporate Register Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – statutory compliance and the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 5 working days of incorporation, the appointed Company Secretary must establish the company register at the registered office, including the share register, director register, minute book, and disclosure of interests register. Prepare and submit the first annual return (Form NZ-ANNUAL with Companies Office) within 10 working days of incorporation to record initial share issues. Ensure the address for service remains compliant (section 186 of the Companies Act 1993). The board must hold its first meeting (or pass a written resolution) to approve the commencement of FMA licensing process, the opening of the segregated client trust accounts, and the adoption of financial reporting framework under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation
Register of shareholders
Register of directors and their consents
Register of beneficial ownership declarations
Minutes of founding board meeting or written resolutions
Annual return form (electronic)
Registered office lease agreement (for statutory records address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first annual return is flagged for omission of beneficial ownership data, the company has 10 working days to file an amendment under section 115 of the Companies Act, without penalty. If the Companies Office indicates compulsory removal for failure to maintain the register, the company may apply for reinstatement (cost: NZD 200) within 12 months of removal, provided the court order is obtained under section 328.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Markets Authority (FMA) of New Zealand, Banking and Insurance conduct division (crowdfunding licensing), and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) for matters of client fund custody; where office premises at the registered address are occupied, the licensing authority is the Auckland Council (Building Consents and Environmental Health) and the New Zealand Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Crowdfunding Service Licence under section 506 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (FMC Act); must be held prior to any offer of equity securities through the digital platform. FMA licensing reference: LM/CF - (year) - (sequence).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA New Zealand) jointly with the Auckland Council – Resource Consents Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 – Low Impact Digital Intermediary Service: Exemption from a Full EIA Report. The operation is office-based and digital. Only an Energy & Carbon Certificate (for office electives) must be registered, but no resource consent is required for the platform operations. However, due to the client fund custody facility and third-party server hosting, an 'Information Technology and Data Management ' prior environmental remainder may trigger a resource consent for an office unit (Building Act 2004 compliance) if the premises changes floor usage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: Standard municipal office (Auckland Council) discharge to sewer, must comply with Trade Waste Bylaw 2015 – BOD < 300 mg/L, suspended solids < 350 mg/L, total petroleum hydrocarbons < 15 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0. Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) from any ventilation/AHU system: emissions capped at 0.5 g/s for a building in compliance with the air-discharge Notice of Auckland Council; Waste handling: e-waste (servers and redundant terminal devices) must be disposed via NZ e-waste certified recycler, certificate issued to the Department of Conservation under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008. Carbon emissions report under the Climate Change Response Act 2002 (as amended by the Climate Change Response (Zero Carbon) Amendment Act 2019), mandatory for the office building; report carbon footprint of the data center hosting the trading engine (must be within New Zealand) at a threshold of < 5,000 t CO2e per annum – initial compliance registration only.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational and physical clearance is delivered by two authorities: (1) Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) – issue a comprehensive Fire Evacuation Scheme approval and Building Fire Permit under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017 and the Building Act 2004; the requirement includes a Fire Protection System containing automatic fire alarm, sprinklers (if floor area > 1,000 m2), and illuminated egress signage inspected at a frequency as per the National Fire Safety Handbook. (2) WorkSafe New Zealand – issue the Graceful Worksafe Occupational Safety & Health Certificate of Compliance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015; requires an on-site-specific operational safety statement and demonstration of worker induction in crowd-funding platform conduct. Additionally, the structural load inspection certificate for the registered office must be issued by a chartered professional engineer (New Zealand) verifying compliance with the Building Code clauses B1 (structure) and E2 (external moisture), and the termination of tenure of the ' business continuity posture' for the server room. As this is an equity crowdfunding platform operating with a minimum number of staff, no high-risk work permits are required; the WorkSafe certificate with the fire sign-off will be kept at the operational address.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake; primary digital portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz); administered by the Commissioner of Inland Revenue under the Tax Administration Act 1994.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident International Company: (1) determine whether the entity carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand or makes supplies subject to New Zealand GST, particularly remote/digital services to New Zealand consumers; (2) for GST purposes, apply for an IRD number and GST registration through myIR using the non-resident company registration pathway; (3) submit certified English incorporation documents, registered agent/office details, ultimate beneficiary/controller declarations, and evidence of the entity's non-resident status; (4) where the entity has no New Zealand taxable activity, no mandatory IRD registration is triggered, but a voluntary GST registration can be made for certain cross-border supplies; (5) for non-resident suppliers of remote and digital services, the simplified offshore supplier registration process in myIR applies once the NZD 60,000 annual threshold is exceeded; (6) upon approval, the IRD number and GST registration effective date are issued in myIR, with returns filed electronically based on the assigned filing frequency.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident International Company: not tax-resident in New Zealand; New Zealand income tax applies only to New Zealand-source income under the territorial rule; an offshore equity crowdfunding portal without a New Zealand branch, permanent establishment, or New Zealand-source intermediary commission is currently outside the New Zealand income tax net, and the entity is not a New Zealand resident taxpayer).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No United States-style check-the-box election exists under New Zealand law; companies are entity-level taxpayers by default. The hybrid mismatch rules in subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007 operate by default to neutralise certain cross-border hybrid arrangements, with limited administrative elections and documentation requirements available before the Commissioner of Inland Revenue. No general election is available to convert a non-resident International Company into a pass-through vehicle for New Zealand income tax purposes; entity classification follows New Zealand domestic law and the entity's actual tax-residence status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a national value-added tax governed by the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; New Zealand has no sub-national or provincial sales taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (NZ$60,000) of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services and digital products to New Zealand consumers; voluntary registration is permitted where taxable supplies are made in New Zealand and the threshold is not exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time invoice clearance by the tax authority, does not require fiscal digital stamping, and does not currently mandate an electronic invoicing API for all taxpayers. GST invoices must contain the prescribed statutory particulars, including seller name and GST registration number, invoice number and date, description of the supply, amount of consideration, and GST charged. Electronic invoices, including those transmitted via the voluntary Peppol network, are valid, but there is no pre-clearance or transaction-level approval procedure by the IRD; periodic GST returns and digital records are submitted through myIR.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supplier has documentary evidence that the supply qualifies as an export: (a) goods physically removed from New Zealand within the prescribed statutory timeframe, provided the supplier holds shipping/customs evidence showing export; (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, provided the services are not performed in connection with New Zealand land and are not otherwise supplied under a contract that gives the supplier a reasonable expectation of use in New Zealand; (c) certain cross-border business-to-business remote and digital services supplied to non-resident recipients where the recipient is not physically in New Zealand. For an equity crowdfunding portal, platform, escrow, and administrative services supplied to non-resident issuers and non-resident investors can qualify for zero-rating where the portal's performance, management, and supply chain are offshore, the recipients are non-resident at the time of supply, and no New Zealand land or physical services are involved.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Airway Bill or equivalent transport document
Executed service agreement or platform terms evidencing the non-resident recipient and offshore supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD subjects zero-rated export claims to strict documentary scrutiny, particularly for offshore digital platforms and financial intermediaries. Where a zero-rating claim is unsupported or fraudulent, the IRD may reassess the supply at the standard 15% GST rate, deny input tax credits, impose use-of-money interest, and apply civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994, including up to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion or similar conduct. Repeat or deliberate conduct can also result in criminal prosecution, significant fines, imprisonment, director and corporate liability, cancellation of pending refunds, retrospective clawback of claimed refunds, and removal from the GST registered persons register.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) — the sole central bank and currency-issuing authority for the NZD, prudential supervisor of registered banks, and the AML/CFT supervisor applicable to NZ banking institutions. New Zealand does not operate a dedicated foreign-exchange-control administration; the Exchange Control Regulations were fully abolished in 1984, so no central-bank approval, surrender, or registration is required for cross-border payments. Adjacent functional supervision is distributed among the Financial Markets Authority (FMA, licensing of the equity crowdfunding intermediary under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013), the Department of Internal Affairs (AML/CFT supervision of non-bank financial institutions and reporting entities), the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (suspicious transaction reporting), and Inland Revenue (non-resident withholding tax and thin-capitalisation enforcement). The Overseas Investment Office administers foreign-investment screening limited to sensitive land and significant business assets and is irrelevant to ordinary treasury flows of a digital crowdfunding platform.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility of the NZD on both current and capital account. The legal distinction between current-account and capital-account items is immaterial for FX control purposes because no exchange-control approval, currency rationing, or registration of cross-border contracts applies. Non-resident shareholders, trust settlors, and lenders may freely convert foreign currency into NZD for equity injections, shareholder advances, inter-company loans, and working capital; the crowdfunding portal may freely remit dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, platform commissions, escrow refunds, and redemption proceeds abroad without Overseas Investment Office consent or Reserve Bank permission. Practical friction points are limited to (i) the AML/CFT Act 2009 wire-transfer originator and beneficiary information duties; (ii) non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) obligations on dividends and interest remitted to non-residents, which require Inland Revenue form IR67 or a valid certificate while the platform applies the correct treaty rate under an applicable double-tax agreement; and (iii) the Part 6 client-money rules of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, which prohibit commingling the platform's operational funds with investor funds held in the qualifying escrow trust account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. There is no statutory timeline within which export proceeds, service fees, platform commissions, or other foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to New Zealand, and there is no prescribed conversion ratio requiring proceeds to be exchanged into NZD. A licensed crowdfunding portal and its foreign issuers may retain receipts in offshore foreign-currency accounts or in approved NZ foreign-currency deposit accounts at Reserve Bank of New Zealand registered banks. The only residual duties are (i) accurate statutory financial reporting of foreign-currency balances under the Companies Act 1993 and applicable financial reporting standards; (ii) compliance with the AML/CFT Act 2009 rules on transmitting originator information for all cross-border wires and making suspicious-transaction reports where required; and (iii) where the non-resident parent trust or International Company benefits from a tax-exempt-zone classification, continued adherence to the evidentiary transparency conditions of the foreign-trust or international-company regime so that bank-account documentation remains accurate, current, and legally enforceable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FMC Act qualifying client-money trust account) plus Operational NZD and Foreign-Currency Accounts
Operational Accounts and Foreign-Currency Accounts; institutional escrow capability via corporate banking and custody desk

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of New Zealand (BNZ, a division of NAB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FMC client-money escrow trust account with integrated Operational Account package
Operational Account only; escrow structuring possible but current risk appetite for crowdfunding intermediaries is narrowed
Primary Operational, GST, and Client Trust Escrow settlement accounts; state-owned domestic bank with strongest alignment to a New Zealand statutory special licence
Operational Account and term-deposit collateral vehicle only; not suitable for core escrow infrastructure

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall viability is LOW as the primary escrow and settlement rail; MEDIUM as an auxiliary FX, payroll, or disbursement utility. Legal constraints: under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008, no person may provide financial services — including money transfer, FX dealing, or payment services — in New Zealand without being registered on the Financial Service Providers Register. Offshore digital EMIs without NZ FSP registration cannot lawfully open NZD transaction accounts for the platform or hold client funds without breaching the FMC Act and the FSP Act. Locally licensed EMIs such as Airwallex NZ can provide multi-currency accounts, but they cannot satisfy the FMA client-money obligation, which requires all equity-crowdfunding investor proceeds to be paid into a single qualifying trust account maintained with an RBNZ-registered bank or licensed non-bank deposit taker. Therefore the statutory escrow rail must sit at a tier-1 commercial bank; fintech EMIs are confined to corporate cards, FX conversion, payroll execution, and sub-account automation that does not touch investor funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: High-touch onboarding mandate applies: at least one director who is an authorised signatory of the International Company and at least one New Zealand-resident compliance officer must attend an in-person corporate onboarding and enhanced-due-diligence interview at the bank's corporate banking centre in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch before account activation. Remote opening is not generally permitted for a High_Risk_Special_License entity ultimately owned by non-residents. In exceptional cases ANZ Bank and Kiwibank will accept hybrid onboarding in which the NZ-resident director appears physically and offshore directors are verified by video-link, provided all offshore directors supply notarised passports, certified proof-of-address from the last six months, and legally apostilled corporate extracts. A registered-agent-only structure, or a fully remote opening where every director is offshore, will be declined by all tier-1 banks. The bank will additionally require an operational street address in New Zealand, an active Companies Office registration with NZBN, an Inland Revenue (IRD) number, GST registration where applicable, the current FMC crowdfunding intermediary licence certificate, and a board resolution designating the AML/CFT compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt-zone International Company with an opaque cross-border ownership chain, including non-resident individuals or trusts holding through nominee, registered-agent, or bare-trust structures — classified as a high-risk jurisdictional overlay triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate register extract and certificate of incumbency issued by the licensed registered agent of the International Company; a legal opinion from a New Zealand-licensed solicitor identifying each natural person with ultimate control; declaration of trust and full trust deed disclosing settlors, protectors, trustees, and beneficiaries; certified passports and proof-of-address for every UBO; sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations supported by 12 months of bank statements for each investing entity; a group-structure chart with natural-person identification at every tier; and an independent professional reference from a member of Chartered Accountants Australia and New Zealand confirming the economic substance and intended activity of the group.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-licensed intermediary engaged in client-money custody — equity crowdfunding is internally classified by bank underwriting teams as a high-risk special-licence business and escalated to the Financial Crime Committee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed FMA crowdfunding intermediary licence under Subpart 2 of Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; the full FMA application pack with business-plan annexes; the Part 6 client-money compliance manual and the signed trust-account deed naming the tier-1 bank as the qualified trust-account provider; an independent assurance report from a licensed auditor confirming the operational segregation and daily reconciliation of investor funds; platform terms and conditions governing release of escrowed contributions only upon successful satisfaction of the offer milestone; a professional-indemnity insurance certificate with cover proportionate to annual committed capital; and the most recent independent AML/CFT audit or compliance report filed in respect of the reporting entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-ticket, mass-retail cross-border inbound wires — thousands of small crowdfunding contributions from offshore retail investors can be mis-profiled as money-mule or transaction-laundering patterns by transaction-monitoring systems.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented transaction-monitoring and velocity-control policy calibrated to the crowdfunding model, including per-investor contribution limits, daily aggregation rules, and rapid-settlement thresholds; a live sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening integration applied both at investor onboarding and on every inbound contribution; a jurisdiction blocklist denying payments from high-risk and non-cooperative territories; KYC and customer-due-diligence thresholds aligned with the AML/CFT Act 2009 and FMA guidance, with identity verification at the NZD 15,000 equivalent trigger and simplified CDD applied only to investors already verified under the FMC crowdfunding rules; an immutable audit log of all screening hits; and a named AML/CFT compliance officer with a DIA-filed suspicious-transaction reporting protocol.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of nominee-shell substance failure: shared registered-office address, no local payroll, no corporate tax footprint, and no physical operational premises for the corporate parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A dedicated business-premise lease or licence in the entity's own name comprising a physical reception, office, and secure server room; local employment contracts and payroll records for at least the compliance officer and operations manager; active NZBN, IRD, and GST registrations aligned to the same legal entity; utility and telecommunications invoices in the entity's own name; the current Companies Register annual return confirming directors and registered office; a letter of engagement with a New Zealand accounting firm evidencing bookkeeping and tax-filing history; and a board resolution approving the banking relationship and designating the responsible manager under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound investment capital into the New Zealand platform should arrive via SWIFT MT103 single credit transfer, or via an ESAS-participant same-day credit push where both banks are New Zealand clearing members. Recommended wire narrative: CONTRIBUTION TO CAPITAL — EQUITY CROWDFUNDING PLATFORM [NZBN] — NON-RESIDENT SHAREHOLDER [NAME] — OPERATIONAL ACCOUNT REFERENCE. The beneficiary account must be the operational non-escrow NZD account; investor client funds must never be routed to the operating account. New Zealand does not use a mandatory Asian-style purpose-code list; banks rely on the SWIFT Remittance Information field, so the narrative must unambiguously convey the capital nature of the transfer, whether equity injection, shareholder loan, or subordinated working-capital facility. During onboarding the bank registers the ultimate remitting entity, and every subsequent wire should originate from the same remitter and carry the same capital reference to avoid compliance holds. Overseas Investment Office consent is not required for a digital crowdfunding intermediary because the business involves no sensitive land and does not approach the NZD 100 million significant-business-asset screening threshold; nevertheless the platform should provide the bank with a standing written confirmation that no sensitive land or over-threshold asset exposure exists. To prevent clearing delays, the remitter should provide in advance a board resolution authorising the capital contribution, the executed subscription or loan agreement, and individual identification and beneficial-ownership documents for the remitting entity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Layered clearing-rail architecture: (1) Domestic issuer disbursements — equity-crowdfunding proceeds payable to New Zealand-resident issuers are cleared through Payments NZ BECS, the Bulk Electronic Clearing System, as same-day or next-day NZD credit pushes to the issuer's nominated account; large-value payments above the bank's cutoff are routed through the RBNZ ESAS real-time gross settlement system for finality. Each disbursement must reference the offer register code and the milestone-release certificate, satisfying the FMC client-money rule that funds are released only when the offer closes successfully and the minimum subscription target is met. (2) Cross-border wires to offshore issuers, suppliers, or advisors — executed via SWIFT MT103 with complete originator and beneficiary identifiers, the ISIN or offer reference, and the purpose narrative EQUITY SUBSCRIPTION PROCEEDS OR PLATFORM COMMISSION UNDER FMC LICENCE NUMBER; the platform must maintain a watchlist of all foreign issuers and perform pre-send sanctions screening because correspondent banks at each intermediary may review the transaction. (3) Commercial letters of credit — where the portal intermediates asset-backed or trade-finance offerings, LCs must be opened through the tier-1 bank's trade-finance desk under UCP600, with the escrow trust account designated as the claiming party and transport documents or service-delivery evidence attached to each presentation; the portal must not create standalone payment undertakings outside the bank's LC and SBLC facilities, as any such undertaking would constitute unlicensed financial-service activity and a breach of the client-money rules. (4) Refund and cancellation flows — investor refunds are made by BECS reversal within ten business days of cancellation and must always be paid from the escrow account, never from the operational account. All rails must support a daily cash ledger reconciled to the trust account in accordance with FMA Part 6 record-keeping standards.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC forward FX contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/AUD, NZD/EUR, NZD/GBP, and NZD/CNY) executed with a tier-1 New Zealand bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement — the standard instrument for hedging anticipated platform-commission income, escrow-currency exposure, and foreign-currency issuer obligations.
FX swaps (spot and forward combination legs) used to manage dual-currency escrow timing mismatches between the investor contribution currency and the issuer disbursement currency.
Cross-currency swaps for long-dated foreign-currency funding of the platform's working capital where the borrowing is denominated in USD, GBP, or EUR and operating revenue is NZD-denominated.
Vanilla currency options (purchased calls and puts) obtained from the New Zealand bank to cap the downside of large issuer-denominated receivables without creating margin-call liquidity risk.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) — technically permissible, but neither standard nor necessary for the NZD because the currency is fully deliverable offshore; where an NDF referencing NZD is nonetheless executed with an offshore counterparty, it will be economically equivalent to a deliverable forward and subject to RBNZ prudential margin and collateral rules if a New Zealand bank or its branch is a counterparty, and to the Financial Market Infrastructures Act 2021 clearing obligations where any applicable clearing threshold is exceeded.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Renewal Fee - International Company (International Companies Act 1981-82, as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission - Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: the annual fee is payable within the window commencing 3 months before and ending 6 months after the incorporation anniversary; the administrative default date is 6 months after the anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of NZ$25 per month (or part-month) of arrears; the Registrar may strike the company off the International Companies Register if the annual fee remains unpaid for 6 months after the due date. Revivification is discretionary and requires payment of all arrears plus penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial-Owner (UBO) Register (bundled attestation to the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission - Beneficial Ownership Registry (lodged through the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Annual Return; no later than 6 months after the incorporation anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or omitted UBO information is a statutory misstatement offence with fines up to NZ$5,000 per offence; persistent non-confirmation may trigger administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Market Services Licence Annual Compliance Return and Sector Levy for Licensed Crowd Funding Service (Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, Part 6)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (New Zealand) - Market Services Licensing Team
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual; the FMA sector levy is invoiced for the 1 July - 30 June levy year and payable within 30 days of invoice; the compliance return is due on the annual licensing anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment or non-filing may result in FMA suspension or cancellation of the crowd funding licence under FMC Act sections 423-433; operating without a current licence is an offence carrying fines up to NZ$500,000 for a body corporate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Compliance Report (Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, section 59A)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (New Zealand) - AML/CFT Supervision
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 August each year, covering the reporting period 1 July - 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is a continuing offence; civil penalty liability up to NZ$200,000 for a reporting entity; FMA may issue remedial directions and revoke the licence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Annual Financial Statements - FMC Reporting Entity (Market Services Licensee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Markets Authority (New Zealand); filed with the New Zealand Companies Office if the entity maintains an NZ branch registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the reporting balance date (for a 31 March balance date: 31 July); FMA extension available only on prior application.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for late filing or absence of a qualified audit opinion; breach of FMC licence conditions may trigger civil penalties and licence cancellation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory if the entity: (i) is an FMC reporting entity as a market services licensee under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; (ii) qualifies as a large company under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 (total assets NZ$60M or more, or total revenue NZ$30M or more); or (iii) is directed by an FMA licence condition to hold an annual certified audit. A passive Cook Islands International Company with no NZ-regulated activity is exempt from audit at the home-jurisdiction level.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: NZ IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted in New Zealand) for all FMA-regulated crowd funding financial statements; the Cook Islands International Companies Act 1981-82 permits IFRS or US GAAP for the entity's home-jurisdiction statutory records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The licensed Cook Islands registered agent maintains the confidential register of beneficial owners. Any share transfer requires the agent's prior due-diligence approval; the updated Register of Members and UBO annexure must be lodged with the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission within 14 days of the transfer. The annual return serves as the annual UBO attestation confirming that the register is complete, current, and accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (with confidential beneficial-owner annexure)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200-3,500 per annum (licensed Cook Islands registered agent, including resident office, registered secretary, and annual return lodging)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-18,000 per annum (FMA-ready NZ IFRS audited financial statements for a small equity crowdfunding portal)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand imposes a 28% corporate income tax rate on the worldwide income of New Zealand tax-resident companies. However, for non-resident-owned International Companies (ICs) structured as exempt or offshore companies and not managed and controlled in New Zealand, no New Zealand corporate income tax is levied on foreign-sourced income. No general statutory tax holiday applies; the R&D Tax Incentive (RDTI) provides a 15% tax credit on eligible R&D expenditure, and the Look-Through Company (LTC) regime may apply to qualifying closely-held entities but is generally incompatible with a crowdfunding portal license.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via myIR (Inland Revenue online portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IR4 must be filed and any terminal tax paid by the standard due date based on the company's balance date. For a standard 31 March balance date, filing is due by 7 July of the following tax year (with extension options under the return filing programme); terminal tax is due by 7 February following the year of assessment. Provisional tax payments are due in three installments: 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May for standard balance dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name and registered tax file number (IRD number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the legal name of the International Company and the IRD number allocated upon incorporation; non-resident companies without a New Zealand taxable presence are generally not required to file if they do not derive New Zealand-sourced income.
State the annual balance date; non-resident ICs deriving no New Zealand taxable income may mark the return as non-resident and nil-return if Inland Revenue has issued an obligation to file.

Report gross assessable income, excluding non-taxable foreign income for exempt offshore ICs; attach schedules of crowdfunding platform fees if treated as attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment.
Aggregate all assessable categories; non-resident companies claiming treaty protection should ensure no New Zealand permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total allowable deductions, including depreciation and interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only against New Zealand-sourced income; expenses allocated to foreign-source income are not deductible for a non-resident IC without NZ PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income / taxable income before tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For nil-return filers, confirm zero taxable income; wrap-up and accrual adjustments are mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credit and RWT/foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach proof of foreign withholding tax credits if claiming credit relief under the applicable double tax agreement (DTA).
Apply 28% rate to net taxable income; assess non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) separately on any distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment of income tax attracts a 1% initial late payment penalty plus an additional 4% after seven days, followed by a further 1% per month (10% cap) on the unpaid amount. Failure to file the IR4 on time imposes a late filing penalty of NZ$250 for small to medium companies, escalating to NZ$500 for larger companies, with possible daily penalties for continued non-compliance under the Tax Administration Act 1994. False statements or omissions may trigger penal taxes of 20% (not deliberate), 40% (abusive), or 150% (evasion) of the tax shortfall.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 28% (Non-Resident Withholding Tax, NRWT) on gross dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company; supplementary dividend regime may effectively increase treaty-rate relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a double tax agreement, the corporate shareholder must be a resident of the treaty country beneficially entitled to the dividend. Inland Revenue requires completion of a statement of entitlement (e.g., IR290 or an equivalent treaty rate claim form), supported by a valid Certificate of Residence (CoR) issued by the foreign tax authority, before the payer applies the reduced NRWT rate. The claim must be lodged with the payer prior to payment; if the lower rate is applied without a valid CoR, the company remains liable for any shortfall NRWT. Where a NZ DTA does not exist, the statutory 28% NRWT applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory NRWT rate is 15% of gross royalties; under most NZ DTAs the rate is reduced to 10% or 5%, depending on the treaty and category of IP. Interest: statutory NRWT is 28% for non-resident lenders not carrying on business in NZ; under most NZ DTAs the rate is reduced to 10% (e.g., Australia, United States, United Kingdom) or 15% for passive interest under some treaties. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) may apply at 2% on interest paid to non-residents if the lender is not associated and the loan is in New Zealand dollars, which substitutes for NRWT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand has not implemented statutory documentation threshold amounts (NZD figures) requiring automatic Local File or Master File preparation; instead, an exemption from contemporaneous documentation applies where the aggregate value of cross-border associated-party transactions is NZD 3 million or less, or the taxpayer is a 'non-active' investor. A Master File and Local File must be prepared and provided to Inland Revenue within 30 days if requested, where the group exceeds NZD 100 million in global turnover and cross-border related-party dealings exceed NZD 10 million, subject to the commissioner's guidelines. All documentation must support an arm's length result for transactions exceeding materiality thresholds set under the OECD transfer pricing guidelines adopted by the Income Tax Act 2007.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand applies general business substance principles. There is no dedicated Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code as in the UAE; however, under the tax avoidance general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in s BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and the interest limitation rules, a company lacking commercial substance with arrangements whose sole or main purpose is tax avoidance will be recharacterized. Crowdfunding portal licensees must maintain genuine operational substance, including registered office, local directors, legal/compliance staffing, and transaction governance, to avoid denial of tax treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) in NZ's DTAs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting crowdfunding commission income, fabricating deductible expenses, or shifting profits to a non-resident IC shell without economic substance to erode the New Zealand taxable base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penal tax of 150% of the tax shortfall under the Tax Administration Act 1994, plus civil penalties up to NZ$250,000 for false returns; criminal conviction for tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to NZ$50,000 per offence. In severe cases, Inland Revenue may seek liquidation of the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit evasion or are knowingly party to a false return can be held personally liable for the company's tax shortfall under the Companies Act 1993 and tax recovery provisions. Directors may face disqualification, personal restitution orders, travel bans by court order, and imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced where the company is used as a façade for deliberate tax wrongdoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach by Equity Crowdfunding Portal (High Risk Special License)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an equity crowdfunding portal under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 without a valid Crowdfunding Service license, or failing to conduct customer due diligence and Politically Exposed Persons determinations on investors and issuing companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a supervised entity that fails to meet AML/CFT obligations faces a civil penalty of up to NZ$2 million for a body corporate for each non-compliance event; the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) may revoke the crowdfunding license and order remediation costs. Criminal sanctions of up to 2 years imprisonment and fines of up to NZ$200,000 for individuals apply for willful misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers are subject to statutory duties under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; civil liability for pecuniary penalties of up to NZ$1 million per director for reckless or dishonest conduct is possible. The FMA may issue banning orders preventing individuals from managing financial services companies; personal liability for investor losses may arise for misstatements in crowdfunding offer documents.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an International Company nominally in New Zealand solely to hold an equity crowdfunding portal license while all key functions, decision-making, custody of escrow funds, and personnel are located outside New Zealand, creating a conduit without real commercial activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The FMA may treat the licence as ineffective and cancel registration; Inland Revenue may apply the GAAR to reallocate income and deny treaty benefits under the PPT. The company's directors may be liable for breach of section 137 of the Companies Act 1993 (reckless trading). Fines up to NZ$200,000 and revocation of the certificate of incorporation under the Companies Office protocols may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors must ensure the company carries on business in a manner that does not create a substantial risk of serious loss to creditors; violation exposes directors to personal liability for debts and restitution orders, plus travel bans and mandatory appearance orders in Inland Revenue investigations. Persistent non-residency of actual decision-makers could render the company managed and controlled in New Zealand, subjecting it to full tax residence and worldwide taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Crowdfunding Activity / Unlicensed Financial Intermediation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an equity crowdfunding portal in New Zealand without holding a Crowdfunding Service provider license under Part 6 of the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, or exceeding licensing scope by facilitating equity issuance without a licensed intermediary
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under the FMCA carry criminal penalties of up to NZ$300,000 for an individual and NZ$2.5 million for a body corporate, plus civil pecuniary penalties of up to NZ$1 million for an individual and NZ$5 million for a body corporate. Orders for restitution to investors, injunctions, and public warning notices may be issued by the FMA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may order civil penalties against every director involved in the contravention; directors are personally liable for such penalties unless they can prove they took all reasonable steps to prevent the breach. They may be subject to banning orders and compensation orders in favor of defrauded investors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising dividends as intercompany loans, failing to withhold NRWT on distributions to non-resident shareholders, or routing compensatory payments through tax haven jurisdictions with no substance to avoid New Zealand dividend withholding tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of 40% for an unacceptable tax position or 150% for evasion, plus interest (use of money interest) on unpaid NRWT. The company as withholding agent is personally liable for all tax not deducted, and late-filed returns invite late filing penalties for every period on the IR4S/RA schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the company's failure to deduct and pay NRWT under a director penalty notice regime; the Commissioner of Inland Revenue may issue a notice requiring payment within 30 days, after which personal recovery action, including bankruptcy proceedings and asset restraining orders, may be pursued.
